skill.displayName: Pet Drying Box Heat Stress Analysis | 宠物烘干箱内热应激预警

llm.summary: The skill does the advertised cloud video analysis, but it also silently creates or reuses account identity, stores access tokens locally, and supports account-scoped history lookup without enough user control.

dimensions.detail: Sending uploaded media or URLs to the configured remote service is expected for server-side analysis, but the code also reads environment identity values, reads workspace data/smyx-api-key.txt, injects account metadata into requests, and contacts a login/register endpoint.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install-time command, background worker, or self-modifying install behavior was found; dependencies are ordinary Python packages, though the documentation understates the dependency and persistence surface.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md documents automatic history queries and internal identity handling, but instructs agents not to ask about or expose identity values while the CLI accepts suppressed --open-id and --api-key parameters.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The common DAO forces a shared workspace data SQLite database, creates or reuses a default user, and can persist token/open_token values without a visible cleanup or explicit consent boundary.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Cloud pet drying-box heat-stress analysis and report listing are largely coherent with the documented purpose, but the runtime also performs silent identity bootstrap, token handling, and history access that materially expand the trust boundary.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use this only if you are comfortable sending pet drying-box videos or URLs to the configured Life Emergence cloud service and with the skill creating/reusing a local account identity, storing tokens in a workspace SQLite database, and querying cloud report history. Prefer a single-user workspace and remove the local data database/tokens if you uninstall or rotate identities.
llm.findings:
[AST7] unexpected: The dynamic ORM filters are generic shared-DAO behavior rather than necessary analysis logic; direct exploitability was not shown, but it adds avoidable breadth around persisted user records.
[LP3] unexpected: The artifact does not provide a clear permissions section matching its network, local file, environment, and database behavior, so the least-privilege concern is supported in part.
[SDI-1] expected: History report listing is not hidden in the inspected SKILL.md; it is documented as an automatic trigger and CLI option.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The generic HTTP CRUD helpers, shared persistence layer, and disabled open_id checks broaden the skill beyond a narrow submit-video-and-return-analysis workflow.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Silent local identity creation/reuse, backend login/register, and local token persistence are concrete artifact-backed concerns for a media-analysis skill.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The external analysis call is expected, but automatic local media saving, hidden identity parameters, and transmitted account metadata are not disclosed with enough privacy detail.
[E1] unexpected: The phoneLogin call sends locally derived identity data to a remote service for silent registration/login; this is not clear from the top-level purpose even though remote analysis itself is expected.
[P2] expected: The zero-width character observed in SKILL.md is part of a visible emoji sequence, not evidence of a hidden instruction.
[YR4] expected: The metadata is long and bilingual but no artifact-backed deceptive tool-metadata behavior was found from the YARA signal alone.
